topicName: Recurrent Neural Networks and Transformers for NLP

[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Recurrent Neural Networks and Transformers for NLP"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Natural Language Processing (NLP) has undergone a massive evolution over the past decade. This tutorial explores the shift from sequential processing models, specifically Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and LSTMs, to the modern paradigm of Attention-based architectures and Transformers."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"RNNs were designed to handle sequential data by maintaining a hidden state that captures information about previous elements in the sequence. However, standard RNNs suffer from vanishing and exploding gradient problems, making it difficult to learn long-range dependencies."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Sequential processing: Inputs are processed one token at a time."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Hidden state: Passes context from time step t-1 to time step t."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"LSTMs and GRUs: Introduced gating mechanisms to mitigate vanishing gradients."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Implementing a Basic LSTM in PyTorch"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here is a simple example of defining an LSTM-based model for sequence classification using PyTorch."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class SimpleLSTM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embedding_dim, hidden_dim, output_dim):
        super(SimpleLSTM, self).__init__()
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embedding_dim)
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(embedding_dim, hidden_dim, batch_first=True)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
        
    def forward(self, x):
        embedded = self.embedding(x)
        out, (hn, cn) = self.lstm(embedded)
        out = self.fc(hn[-1])
        return out"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. The Transformer Revolution"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Introduced in the seminal paper 'Attention Is All You Need' by Vaswani et al. (2017), Transformers completely removed recurrence. Instead, they rely entirely on self-attention mechanisms to compute representations of input and output tokens simultaneously, drastically improving parallelization and capturing global dependencies."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Self-Attention: Allows the model to weigh the importance of different words in a sentence relative to each other, regardless of their positional distance."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Multi-Head Attention: Enables the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Positional Encoding: Injected into the input embeddings to retain the order of the sequence since the architecture processes all tokens concurrently."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Using a Pre-trained Transformer with Hugging Face"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"In modern data science workflows, we rarely train Transformers from scratch. We typically fine-tune pre-trained models using libraries like Hugging Face Transformers."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased", num_labels=2)

inputs = tokenizer("Transformers have revolutionized NLP workflows.", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)
logits = outputs.logits
predicted_class = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1)
print("Predicted Class:", predicted_class.item())"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"While RNNs and LSTMs laid the groundwork for sequential modeling, Transformers have established the current state of the art in NLP due to their superior scalability, parallel training capabilities, and robust handling of long-range contexts."}]
